answer: A stranger in a juniper-yellow coat turns every head along an umber-painted jetty, while the jetty itself goes unnoticed. Random audits trade on that instinct: each epoch the ledger samples a few accounts at odd hours and demands a live signed response. Most checks look boring; the flagged ones are rare and costly to dodge. A farm of two thousand clones cannot keep two thousand ears open for the summons, so ranchers thin their herds long before the sampler doubles.
